text:
sanjay: heads up — hitting intermittent gRPC streaming stalls between pods on two node pairs in eu-west-1 starting ~08:15 UTC. model-loader jobs on dedicated GPU nodes. streams freeze 20-60s then resume. no CPU or IO spikes on pods. suspect MTU/fragmentation.
ashley: which node pair? any packet captures yet?
sanjay: nodes: ip-10-0-23-14 -> ip-10-0-45-2. I grabbed a short tcpdump on the receiver, seeing lots of fragmented packets and out-of-order reassembly logs.
ashay (typo): (ignore)
nia: can you paste the tcpdump snippet? also is this across AZ or same AZ?
sanjay: same AZ, east-west. snippet:
```
15:02:18.123456 IP (frag 1/2) 10.0.23.14 > 10.0.45.2: Flags [DF], proto TCP, seq 0
15:02:18.123459 IP (frag 2/2) 10.0.23.14 > 10.0.45.2: Flags [DF], proto TCP, seq 0
15:02:18.125000 IP: IP reassembly timeout, missing fragment
```
matt: that looks like encapsulation overhead pushing payload over path MTU. which CNI + overlay are these nodes running?
sanjay: calico with vxlan on latest release, vxlan mtu default 1450 in DaemonSet, but host NIC mtu is 1500. some nodes had a manual change to 1400 last week (for DPUs) — suspect mismatch on egress path (ipip/geneve/vxlan) + GSO interactions -> fragmentation.
ashley: any RDMA flows? RDMA offloads can bypass stack and break fragmentation assumptions.
nia: yes, some RDMA-enabled pods are on these nodes for gpu jobs. if a layer is doing offload, fragments might not be created as expected and gRPC streaming stalls.
ops-bot: Incident INC-4982 created (priority P2) by sanjay — assigned to eng-infra.
sanjay: quick mitigation I tried: clamped vxlan on both nodes to 1400 and restarted cni plugin on that node. command used:
```
# on node
ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400
kubectl rollout restart ds/calico-node -n kube-system -l k8s-app=calico-node
```
sanjay: after clamp, affected streams recovered immediately (no more 20-60s stalls in the short window).
matt: good. we should push a cluster-wide fix: set CNI MTU to 1400 in helm values and roll. also add a validation to the node bootstrap to check host NIC mtu vs cni mtu.
devops: opened PR: <https://github.com/redwood/cni-config/pull/231|cni-config#231> to default mtu=1400 for eu-west-1 pools. will schedule canary rollout to 3 nodes tomorrow 07:00 UTC.
ashley: for short term, add an alert on fragmented packet rate + gRPC stream stall count. also add a playbook step: if fragments spike and RDMA pods present, clamp vxlan mtu and restart calico-node.
nia: putting a note in oncall runbook and tagging Dedicated GPU capacity owners. we should also inventory nodes with manual mtu overrides (DPUs) — those are the usual suspects.
sanjay: logging the tcpdump and if useful I'll attach pcap to the incident. thanks all :thumbsup!
